structured_output.summary: The wire-and-compatibility chunk is implemented tightly and backed by real execution evidence. profiles.rs changes exactly the two request-schema arguments (lines 91, 214) and keeps frozen response roots and operation names; a dedicated regression proves that byte-exact delta. New Rust tests cover create/update/get/list/paged paths with defaults on and off, pre-auth rejection of newly modeled invalid values (zero token/wire calls), typed-over-extension precedence, lossless null/unsupported responses, and the 0.35.0 oracle corpus; all ran under 1.89.0 and 1.99.0 with the offline example executed. Docs (DIRECTIONAL_PROFILES, CHANGELOG, STABILITY, LIVE_ACCEPTANCE) are candid and receipt-bound; the fresh read-only receipt honestly records 1 verified method. Main gap: phase 27's command set drops the entire test_typescript035_governance.py suite, removing several supplemental-source tamper regressions from the cumulative gate.

findings.description: commands_for(27) excludes the whole test_typescript035_governance.py suite from the glob-expanded unit-test set. Only two of its tests genuinely conflict with post-implementation state (test_frozen_contracts_and_planning_sdk_bytes asserts crates/scm-sdk equals 578f2e6, and test_independent_dependency_checks_and_original_gate_remain expects phase 26 to be an unmet predecessor). Excluding the file also drops still-valid supplemental-source regressions from the phase-27 gate: forged self-consistent manifest/git origin (line 98), license identity and digest (line 52), baseline ledger tamper and pinned Zod dependency (line 67), added-file/symlink rejection (lines 123, 167), and private-receipt post-check tamper (line 29). verify-contracts.py --self-test and verify_typescript035_source.py --check still run and cover part of this, but the fail-closed proofs for the 0.35.0 pins are no longer re-executed.
findings.required_fix: Split the two phase-26-only assertions into a separate module (or gate them on the active phase) and include the remaining governance regressions in commands_for(27), rather than excluding the file by name.

findings.description: The read-only receipt validator accepts either HISTORICAL_READ_ONLY_LIMITATIONS or READ_ONLY_LIMITATIONS, so `live_evidence.py --check` alone would pass a phase-27 receipt that omits the required endpoint-profile limitation. Only red_team_management.py --check --current-source-compatibility (verify_service_qualification, line 801) enforces the complete list.
findings.required_fix: Require READ_ONLY_LIMITATIONS for non-phase-24 (current-source) receipts in live_evidence.load, keeping the historical list accepted only for the archived phase-24 receipt path.

findings.description: sourceBindings pin only the upstream model file and the four generator tools. The delivered wire-layer artifacts for this chunk (crates/scm-sdk/src/airs/management/profiles.rs, tests/typescript035_models.rs, examples/directional_profiles.rs) are not hash-bound in the additive ledger; they are covered indirectly by tools/test_typescript035_implementation.py and the phase source fingerprint.
findings.required_fix: Add the profile client, directional model test and example to the parity ledger sourceBindings so the ledger alone pins the delivered implementation, mirroring red_team_management.py's management_runtime_evidence source bindings.

findings.description: The Rust builder snippet (including the `# Ok::<(), scm_sdk::Error>(())` doctest idiom) is in a standalone markdown file that no crate target includes, so it is never compiled; it can drift from the API. The equivalent flow is compiled and executed via examples/directional_profiles.rs.
findings.required_fix: Either include this guide through #![doc = include_str!(..)] so the snippet is doctested, or drop the doctest-only hidden line and reference the compiled example instead.

tools/check_phase.py:835-869 plus tools/test_phase_checkpoint.py (12 tests incl. later-command receipt mutation, archive bytes, stale/future windows, symlink) make --resume reuse fail closed; review_phase.py:220 rechecks receipt bindings at review time.
limitations: Read-only review: I could not run git, cargo or the phase driver, so command exit codes, test counts and source fingerprints were assessed from the recorded receipts (docs/reviews/phase-27-chunk-wire-and-compatibility-attempt-01.checks.json and docs/checks/phase-27-rust-*-management.json) rather than re-executed.
I did not recompute SHA-256 digests, so pin consistency (e.g. qualification.json's live-evidence hash, parity ledger sourceBindings) rests on the recorded passing checks that verify them.

Directional create/update were never exercised against a real tenant; the current receipt verifies only OAuth token exchange, and the four Red Team probes returned 403. Directional live acceptance remains unverified, as the docs state.

No package-consumer build against the changed source runs in phase 27 (check-management-package.py and --verify-package-receipts are deliberately excluded); management_consumers.py --check reports executionClaimed false. That evidence is deferred to phase 28 per the plan and I did not judge it here.

I reviewed only the wire-and-compatibility chunk scope; generated model/validation correctness was assessed through the compiler, selected generated declarations (generated.rs:4456-4569, 13369-13580) and the independent fixture/oracle checks, not a full audit of the models-and-validation chunk.
I did not read .local/typescript or any credential/tenant-registration material; the pinned contracts/sources/typescript-0.35.0 tree was used as the authoritative upstream input.
